cards.front: How does a beta cell turn a rise in blood glucose into insulin release?
cards.back: Glucose enters through **GLUT2** and is phosphorylated by **glucokinase**. Its metabolism raises **ATP**, which closes **ATP-sensitive K+ channels**. The cell **depolarizes**, **voltage-gated Ca2+ channels** open, and Ca2+ influx triggers **insulin exocytosis**.
cards.back_pt: A glicose entra pelo **GLUT2** e é fosforilada pela **glicoquinase**. Seu metabolismo aumenta o **ATP**, que fecha os **canais de K+ sensíveis ao ATP**. A célula **despolariza**, os **canais de Ca2+ dependentes de voltagem** se abrem e o influxo de Ca2+ desencadeia a **exocitose de insulina**.

cards.front: How does insulin increase glucose uptake, and which tissues depend on it?
cards.back: Insulin binds a **receptor tyrosine kinase**. Its signaling moves **GLUT4** transporters to the cell membrane. This insulin-dependent uptake occurs in **skeletal muscle** and **adipose tissue**. Brain, RBCs, liver and beta cells take up glucose without insulin.
cards.back_pt: A insulina se liga a um **receptor tirosina-quinase**. Sua sinalização leva transportadores **GLUT4** para a membrana celular. Essa captação dependente de insulina ocorre no **músculo esquelético** e no **tecido adiposo**. Cérebro, hemácias, fígado e células beta captam glicose sem insulina.

cards.back: **T-cell-mediated autoimmune destruction** of beta cells, linked to **HLA-DR3** and **HLA-DR4**. Islets show **insulitis** (lymphocytic infiltrate). **Islet autoantibodies** (anti-GAD65, anti-insulin, anti-IA-2) appear years before hyperglycemia; they are markers, while T cells do the damage.
cards.back_pt: **Destruição autoimune das células beta mediada por linfócitos T**, associada a **HLA-DR3** e **HLA-DR4**. As ilhotas mostram **insulite** (infiltrado linfocitário). **Autoanticorpos anti-ilhota** (anti-GAD65, anti-insulina, anti-IA-2) surgem anos antes da hiperglicemia; são marcadores, e o dano é feito pelas células T.

cards.front: Which two defects cause type 2 diabetes, and what is seen in its islets?
cards.back: **Insulin resistance** (closely linked to **central obesity**) plus progressive **beta-cell failure**. Hyperglycemia appears when insulin output can no longer compensate. Islets show **amyloid** made of **amylin (IAPP)**. Twin studies show a stronger genetic influence than in type 1.
cards.back_pt: **Resistência à insulina** (muito ligada à **obesidade central**) mais **falência progressiva das células beta**. A hiperglicemia aparece quando a secreção de insulina não consegue mais compensar. As ilhotas mostram **amiloide** formado por **amilina (IAPP)**. Estudos com gêmeos mostram influência genética maior que no tipo 1.

cards.front: How does insulin deficiency lead to the acidosis and the breathing pattern of DKA?
cards.back: Low insulin with high **glucagon** drives **lipolysis**. The liver turns the free fatty acids into **ketone bodies** (acetoacetate, **β-hydroxybutyrate**). The result is a **high anion gap metabolic acidosis**, deep rapid **Kussmaul breathing**, and **fruity breath** from acetone.
cards.back_pt: Insulina baixa com **glucagon** alto estimula a **lipólise**. O fígado converte os ácidos graxos livres em **corpos cetônicos** (acetoacetato, **β-hidroxibutirato**). O resultado é **acidose metabólica com ânion gap elevado**, respiração profunda e rápida de **Kussmaul** e **hálito cetônico** (frutado) pela acetona.

cards.front: Why is ketosis minimal in hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS)?
cards.back: HHS usually occurs in **type 2 diabetes**. **Residual insulin** is enough to block **lipolysis and ketogenesis** but not to control glucose. Glucose rises very high, **osmotic diuresis** causes **severe dehydration** and **hyperosmolality**, and confusion or coma follows.
cards.back_pt: O EHH costuma ocorrer no **diabetes tipo 2**. A **insulina residual** basta para bloquear a **lipólise e a cetogênese**, mas não para controlar a glicemia. A glicose sobe muito, a **diurese osmótica** causa **desidratação grave** e **hiperosmolalidade**, e surgem confusão mental ou coma.

cards.front: How does nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy differ from proliferative retinopathy?
cards.back: **Nonproliferative**: weak, leaky capillaries cause **microaneurysms**, **dot-blot hemorrhages**, **hard exudates** and **macular edema**. **Proliferative**: retinal **ischemia** releases **VEGF**, so fragile **new vessels** grow. They bleed into the vitreous and can cause **tractional retinal detachment**.
cards.back_pt: **Não proliferativa**: capilares frágeis e permeáveis causam **microaneurismas**, **hemorragias puntiformes e em borrão** (*dot-blot*), **exsudatos duros** e **edema macular**. **Proliferativa**: a **isquemia** retiniana libera **VEGF**, e crescem **neovasos** frágeis. Eles sangram no vítreo e podem causar **descolamento tracional de retina**.

cards.front: Why are infants of mothers with poorly controlled diabetes large at birth and hypoglycemic after delivery?
cards.back: Maternal **glucose crosses the placenta**, but insulin does not. Fetal **beta-cell hyperplasia** produces **hyperinsulinemia**, and insulin is anabolic, causing **macrosomia**. At birth, the glucose supply stops while insulin stays high, causing **neonatal hypoglycemia**.
cards.back_pt: A **glicose materna atravessa a placenta**, mas a insulina não. A **hiperplasia das células beta** fetais produz **hiperinsulinemia**, e a insulina é anabólica, causando **macrossomia**. Ao nascer, o aporte de glicose cessa enquanto a insulina segue alta, causando **hipoglicemia neonatal**.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has had 2 days of vomiting and abdominal pain. She stopped her insulin because she was not eating. She is drowsy, her breathing is deep and rapid, and her breath has a fruity smell. Blood pressure is 98/60 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. Her mucous membranes are dry. Serum studies show glucose 520 mg/dL, Na+ 131 mEq/L, K+ 5.8 mEq/L, Cl- 95 mEq/L and HCO3- 8 mEq/L. Arterial pH is 7.20. Urine ketones are strongly positive. Which statement best describes her potassium balance?
choices: Total body potassium is high because her kidneys cannot excrete potassium
Total body potassium is normal, and serum potassium reflects it accurately
Total body potassium is low, and serum potassium will fall when insulin is given
Total body potassium is high because of potassium release from injured muscle
Total body potassium is normal, and the high serum level comes from low aldosterone
questions.explanation: This is **DKA**: the anion gap is 131 − (95 + 8) = **28 mEq/L**. **Insulin deficiency** and **hyperosmolality** (more than the acidosis itself) shift K+ out of cells, so serum K+ is high. Meanwhile, **osmotic diuresis** and vomiting have depleted **total body K+**. Insulin drives K+ back into cells, so serum K+ can drop quickly during treatment. The first choice is tempting, but her kidneys are losing potassium, not retaining it.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **CAD**: o ânion gap é 131 − (95 + 8) = **28 mEq/L**. A **deficiência de insulina** e a **hiperosmolalidade** (mais do que a própria acidose) deslocam o K+ para fora das células, e por isso o K+ sérico está alto. Ao mesmo tempo, a **diurese osmótica** e os vômitos depletaram o **K+ corporal total**. A insulina leva o K+ de volta para dentro das células, então o K+ sérico pode cair rapidamente durante o tratamento. A primeira alternativa é tentadora, mas os rins dela estão perdendo potássio, e não o retendo.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man has had fatigue, thirst and frequent urination for 3 months. His BMI is 34 kg/m2, and he has dark, velvety skin on the back of his neck. His father and brother have diabetes. Fasting plasma glucose is 182 mg/dL on two separate days. Urine ketones are negative, and islet autoantibodies are not detected. If his pancreatic islets were examined, which finding would be most likely?
choices: Iron deposits in islet and acinar cells
Loss of acinar tissue with fibrosis and calcification
questions.explanation: Obesity, **acanthosis nigricans** (a sign of insulin resistance), a strong family history and no ketosis or autoantibodies point to **type 2 diabetes**. Its islets typically contain **amyloid** formed from **amylin (IAPP)**, which is co-secreted with insulin and adds to beta-cell loss. **Insulitis** (lymphocytic infiltration) is the most tempting choice, but it is the lesion of autoimmune **type 1** diabetes. Beta-cell hyperplasia is the lesion of infants of diabetic mothers, iron suggests hemochromatosis, and fibrosis with calcification suggests chronic pancreatitis.
questions.explanation_pt: Obesidade, **acantose nigricans** (sinal de resistência à insulina), forte história familiar e ausência de cetose e de autoanticorpos indicam **diabetes tipo 2**. Suas ilhotas costumam conter **amiloide** formado por **amilina (IAPP)**, que é cossecretada com a insulina e contribui para a perda de células beta. A **insulite** (infiltrado linfocitário) é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas é a lesão do **diabetes tipo 1** autoimune. A hiperplasia de células beta é a lesão do filho de mãe diabética, ferro sugere hemocromatose, e fibrose com calcificação sugere pancreatite crônica.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman who works as a nurse is brought to the emergency department after she was found confused at work. Fingerstick glucose is 36 mg/dL, and she recovers quickly with IV dextrose. She has had two similar episodes in the past month. She does not have diabetes, but her mother has type 2 diabetes treated with insulin. Blood drawn before the dextrose shows a very high insulin level, a low C-peptide and a low proinsulin. A sulfonylurea screen is negative. What is the most likely cause of her hypoglycemia?
questions.explanation: Beta cells cleave **proinsulin** into insulin and **C-peptide** in equal amounts, so C-peptide marks **endogenous** insulin. Injected insulin contains no C-peptide and suppresses the beta cells, giving **high insulin with low C-peptide and proinsulin**. **Insulinoma** is the most tempting choice, but it raises insulin, C-peptide and proinsulin together. Sulfonylureas give the same pattern as insulinoma, and the negative drug screen excludes them.
questions.explanation_pt: As células beta clivam a **pró-insulina** em insulina e **peptídeo C** em quantidades iguais, então o peptídeo C marca a insulina **endógena**. A insulina injetada não contém peptídeo C e suprime as células beta, resultando em **insulina alta com peptídeo C e pró-insulina baixos**. O **insulinoma** é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas eleva insulina, peptídeo C e pró-insulina juntos. As sulfonilureias dão o mesmo padrão do insulinoma, e a pesquisa negativa do fármaco as exclui.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has had type 2 diabetes for 15 years, with poor control. He has blurred vision in both eyes and burning pain with numbness in both feet. Slit-lamp examination shows bilateral lens opacities. Vibration and pinprick sensation are reduced in a stocking distribution, and ankle reflexes are absent. Increased flow of glucose through a pathway started by which enzyme best explains both his lens and nerve findings?
questions.explanation: The lens, Schwann cells and retina take up glucose without insulin. With high glucose, **aldose reductase** reduces it to **sorbitol**, using NADPH. These cells have little **sorbitol dehydrogenase**, so sorbitol is trapped and pulls in water, causing **osmotic damage** (**cataracts**, **neuropathy**). Sorbitol dehydrogenase is the most tempting choice, but it removes sorbitol by converting it to fructose; its low activity allows the build-up rather than causing it.
questions.explanation_pt: O cristalino, as células de Schwann e a retina captam glicose sem insulina. Com glicose alta, a **aldose redutase** a reduz a **sorbitol**, usando NADPH. Essas células têm pouca **sorbitol desidrogenase**, então o sorbitol fica retido e atrai água, causando **lesão osmótica** (**catarata**, **neuropatia**). A sorbitol desidrogenase é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas ela remove o sorbitol, convertendo-o em frutose; sua baixa atividade permite o acúmulo, mas não o causa.

notes.title: Diabetes mellitus: physiology, types, emergencies and complications
notes.body_md:
## Insulin and glucagon

- Beta cells sense glucose through **GLUT2**, **glucokinase**, a rise in ATP and closure of **K-ATP channels**; Ca2+ influx releases insulin.
- **Proinsulin** is cut into insulin and **C-peptide** in equal amounts.
- **Insulin** (receptor tyrosine kinase): **GLUT4** uptake in muscle and fat; builds glycogen, fat and protein; moves K+ into cells.
- **Glucagon** (Gs-cAMP, mainly liver): **glycogenolysis**, **gluconeogenesis**, **ketogenesis**.

## Diagnosis

- Fasting glucose **≥126 mg/dL**, **HbA1c ≥6.5%**, 2-hour OGTT glucose **≥200 mg/dL**, or random glucose **≥200 mg/dL** with classic symptoms. Without symptoms, a repeat test confirms.
- **HbA1c** is glycated hemoglobin and reflects about 3 months. It is falsely low when RBC survival is short (hemolysis, blood loss) and unreliable in some **hemoglobinopathies**.

## Types

- **Type 1**: T-cell autoimmunity, **HLA-DR3/DR4**, autoantibodies, **insulitis**; absolute insulin deficiency; prone to **DKA**.
- **Type 2**: **insulin resistance** plus **beta-cell failure**; obesity; islet **amyloid (IAPP)**; strong family history; prone to **HHS**.
- **MODY**: autosomal dominant single-gene beta-cell defects; *GCK* (glucokinase) mutations cause mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia.

## Emergencies

- **DKA**: hyperglycemia, ketones, **high anion gap acidosis**, **Kussmaul breathing**, fruity breath, abdominal pain. Serum K+ is often high, but **total body K+ is low**. Triggers: infection, missed insulin, myocardial infarction.
- **HHS**: extreme hyperglycemia, high osmolality, severe dehydration, confusion; little or no ketosis.

## Chronic complications

- **Nonenzymatic glycation** forms advanced glycation end products: thick basement membranes, **hyaline arteriolosclerosis**.
- **Aldose reductase** makes sorbitol in lens, nerves and retina: **cataracts**, **neuropathy**.
- **Retinopathy**: nonproliferative, then proliferative (**VEGF**, new vessels).
- **Nephropathy**: see the glomerular disease block.
- **Macrovascular**: coronary, cerebral and peripheral atherosclerosis. Also **gastroparesis** and more **infections**.

## Hypoglycemia

- High insulin, **low C-peptide**: injected insulin.
- High insulin, **C-peptide and proinsulin**: insulinoma or **sulfonylurea** (a drug screen separates them).

## Pregnancy

- Maternal hyperglycemia causes fetal hyperinsulinemia: **macrosomia**, then **neonatal hypoglycemia**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Insulina e glucagon

- As células beta detectam a glicose via **GLUT2**, **glicoquinase**, aumento do ATP e fechamento dos **canais K-ATP**; o influxo de Ca2+ libera insulina.
- A **pró-insulina** é clivada em insulina e **peptídeo C** em quantidades iguais.
- **Insulina** (receptor tirosina-quinase): captação via **GLUT4** no músculo e no tecido adiposo; síntese de glicogênio, gordura e proteína; leva K+ para dentro das células.
- **Glucagon** (Gs-AMPc, principalmente fígado): **glicogenólise**, **gliconeogênese**, **cetogênese**.

## Diagnóstico

- Glicemia de jejum **≥126 mg/dL**, **HbA1c ≥6,5%**, glicemia de 2 horas no TOTG **≥200 mg/dL** ou glicemia casual **≥200 mg/dL** com sintomas clássicos. Sem sintomas, um novo teste confirma.
- A **HbA1c** é a hemoglobina glicada e reflete cerca de 3 meses. Fica falsamente baixa quando a sobrevida das hemácias é curta (hemólise, perda sanguínea) e não é confiável em algumas **hemoglobinopatias**.

## Tipos

- **Tipo 1**: autoimunidade de células T, **HLA-DR3/DR4**, autoanticorpos, **insulite**; deficiência absoluta de insulina; propenso à **CAD**.
- **Tipo 2**: **resistência à insulina** mais **falência das células beta**; obesidade; **amiloide (IAPP)** nas ilhotas; forte história familiar; propenso ao **EHH**.
- **MODY**: defeitos monogênicos das células beta, autossômicos dominantes; mutações do *GCK* (glicoquinase) causam hiperglicemia de jejum leve e estável.

## Emergências

- **CAD**: hiperglicemia, cetonas, **acidose com ânion gap elevado**, **respiração de Kussmaul**, hálito cetônico, dor abdominal. O K+ sérico costuma estar alto, mas o **K+ corporal total está baixo**. Desencadeantes: infecção, omissão de insulina, infarto do miocárdio.
- **EHH**: hiperglicemia extrema, osmolalidade alta, desidratação grave, confusão mental; pouca ou nenhuma cetose.

## Complicações crônicas

- A **glicação não enzimática** forma produtos finais de glicação avançada: membranas basais espessas, **arteriolosclerose hialina**.
- A **aldose redutase** produz sorbitol no cristalino, nos nervos e na retina: **catarata**, **neuropatia**.
- **Retinopatia**: não proliferativa e, depois, proliferativa (**VEGF**, neovasos).
- **Nefropatia**: ver o bloco de doenças glomerulares.
- **Macrovasculares**: aterosclerose coronariana, cerebral e periférica. Também **gastroparesia** e mais **infecções**.

## Hipoglicemia

- Insulina alta, **peptídeo C baixo**: insulina injetada.
- Insulina, **peptídeo C e pró-insulina** altos: insulinoma ou **sulfonilureia** (a pesquisa do fármaco os diferencia).

## Gestação

- A hiperglicemia materna causa hiperinsulinemia fetal: **macrossomia** e, depois, **hipoglicemia neonatal**.
